# Drone Invaders

Shooter arcade estilo años 80: bajá los drones que forman una figura sobre el techo del estadio.

- Un solo archivo estático: `index.html` (HTML, CSS y JS sin dependencias de build).
- Controles: tocá y arrastrá en el celular (dispara solo), o ← → y Espacio en el teclado.

## Power-ups

Algunos drones derribados sueltan una cápsula (más seguido si estaban en picada). Atrapala con la nave:

| Cápsula | Efecto | Duración |
|---|---|---|
| **R** amarilla | Tiro rápido: dispara el doble de rápido y con más pelotas en el aire | 10 s |
| **T** violeta | Tiro triple: tres pelotas en abanico | 10 s |
| **L** verde | Cámara lenta: drones y bombas van más despacio (la nave y tus tiros no) | 8 s |
| **E** celeste | Escudo: absorbe un golpe | 15 s o hasta el golpe |
| **+** roja | Vida extra (máximo 5) | — |

Los power-ups activos se ven abajo a la izquierda con su tiempo restante. Se combinan entre sí y se pierden al perder una vida.

## Deploy en Vercel

Importá el repo en Vercel con el preset **Other**, sin build command ni output directory. Vercel sirve `index.html` desde la raíz.

## Correr localmente

Abrí `index.html` en el navegador, o servilo con `npx serve .`

## Imágenes para redes

En `img/share/` están las imágenes para compartir, generadas a partir de la escena real del juego:

| Archivo | Tamaño | Uso |
|---|---|---|
| `og.png` | 1200×630 | Vista previa del link (WhatsApp, X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack) |
| `post-square.png` | 1080×1080 | Post de Instagram / Facebook |
| `story.png` | 1080×1920 | Historia de Instagram / WhatsApp |
| `header-x.png` | 1500×500 | Portada de perfil en X |
| `cover-facebook.png` | 1640×624 | Portada de página de Facebook |

Para regenerarlas (necesita Google Chrome): `tools/covers.sh`

Instance

An open-source game development environment: a visual editor and a game engine for .gmk and .gm81 projects.

Try it in your browser · Download · Manual

Instance is a classic 2D game creation tool, written from scratch in Rust. You build games from sprites, objects, events and rooms, with drag-and-drop actions or the GML scripting language. It opens existing `.gmk` and `.gm81` projects and plays them the way you remember, on Windows, macOS, Linux and in the browser. Older games rely on all kinds of engine quirks: the order events run in, the exact random number generator, how `sound_isplaying` lags behind the audio. A tiny living civilization inside a mysterious box. Godot 4.7.2 · GDScript · Android-first.

## Run

Open the folder in Godot 4.7.2 and press **F5** (main scene: `scenes/main/boot.tscn`), or:

```sh
godot --path .
```

The game continues the most recently saved world; the first launch creates one.
Saves live in `user://saves/<world_id>/` — on Windows:
`%APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\My World in a Box\saves\`.

### Desktop controls (development)

| Input | Gesture |
|---|---|
| Left click / drag | Tap (the world answers: dust, ripples, a shaken tree…) / one-finger drag (mouse emulates touch) |
| Double click | Double tap: look at the thing under the cursor, or zoom toward open ground |
| Hold left button on a rock, then drag | Pick it up and carry it; release to drop |
| Hold left button | Long press: menu for what is under the cursor (Inspect / Touch / Look closer) |
| Mouse wheel | Pinch zoom at the cursor |
| Right drag | Two-finger drag |
| F3 | Toggle debug overlay (debug builds; on device: three-finger tap) |

Release builds: tap the version label 7 times within 3 s to unlock debug tools.

# The Well-Tempered Game

A videogame for learning and practising species counterpoint.

## Contents so far

- `data/fux/two-voice/fux-two-voice.json` is the game dataset: the 46 two-voice exercises from
  Fux's *Gradus ad Parnassum* (Part I), with Fux's original solutions, interval annotations and a
  cantus-firmus catalogue. `data/fux/two-voice/README.md` documents the schema and provenance, and
  `VALIDATION.md` holds the validation report.
- `data/sources/fux-species/` is a pinned, vendored copy of the source files (Four Score and More /
  Open Music Theory, CC0).
- `tools/fux_import/` holds the importer (standard-library Python) and the validator. The validator
  can optionally cross-check against music21.
- `src/music/fux/` is the typed runtime access layer: `FuxRepository` and the player-solution model.

```sh
npm install
npm run data:fetch    # re-vendor the pinned upstream commit (needs git + network)
npm run data          # build + validate (fails loudly on any error)
npm run typecheck && npm test
```

The importer needs Python ≥ 3.10. `pip install music21` enables the independent cross-parse in
validation. Node ≥ 22.18 runs the TypeScript sources directly.

desc: Physically based acoustics for Minecraft (Fabric 26.3, client only): occlusion, sound around corners, raytraced reverb, HRTF
readme:
# Earshot

Physically based acoustics for Minecraft 26.3: occlusion, sound bending around corners, raytraced reverb and echo, and binaural (HRTF) audio. It applies to the game's own sounds and, through [Yak VC](https://github.com/desocketed/yakvc)'s voice sink ([desocketed/yakvc#174](https://github.com/desocketed/yakvc/issues/174)), to proximity voice. It is a client-only Fabric mod.

Status: **alpha (M5)**. Game sounds are muffled by what is in the way, come round corners from the opening they pass through, fade with air absorption, shift with Doppler, and are muffled underwater. Each also feeds a reverb measured from the space around you: a convolution with an impulse response synthesized from the room where OpenAL Soft has the effect, EAX reverb otherwise. Yak VC's voices, with its voice sink, get the same treatment. Settings are under Options → Music & Sounds → Acoustics….

**Players:** see the [user guide](docs/GUIDE.md). [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) has the design, the milestones and the measurements so far.

## How it works

- **Simulation (Rust).** A Rust engine, loaded through Java's Foreign Function & Memory API, keeps a voxel copy of the blocks around you. It traces rays through them to work out occlusion, the paths sound takes around walls, and the reverb of the space you're in.
- **Rendering (OpenAL Soft).** The OpenAL Soft that ships with Minecraft renders the result:
  - EFX filters for muffling;
  - EAX or convolution reverb, with impulse responses synthesized from the raytrace;
  - HRTF for direction.

## Development

You need JDK 25 and rustup. rustup reads `rust-toolchain.toml`. Linux cross builds also need `cargo-zigbuild`.

```sh
cargo test --workspace          # Rust crates
cargo xtask header              # regenerate crates/earshot-ffi/include/earshot.h after changing the C ABI
cd mod && ./gradlew runClient   # builds the native library for this machine and starts the game
cd mod && ./gradlew alBench     # what OpenAL Soft costs with Earshot's effects (M0)
cargo xtask dist                # the mod jar in dist/, with this machine's native library only
```

Building in a VM, from a folder shared with the host over VirtioFS, needs two settings:
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` on a local disk, because rustc can't memory-map its fresh objects there.
- `-Pearshot.runDir=<local dir>` for the game runs, because Minecraft can't lock its saves there.

readme:
# Puckbound

3-on-3 arcade hockey RPG for phones and browsers. You run the Snowcrest Foxes (rename them in the club editor), any Frostline club, or a club of your own through the Frostline league and up the country's divisions. Plain HTML5 canvas and ES modules, with no build step and no dependencies.

## Run it

```bash
cd glacial-strikers
python3 tools/serve.py 8080
```

Open http://localhost:8080 on this computer. To play on a phone on the same Wi‑Fi, open `http://<this-computer's-IP>:8080` (on a Mac, `ipconfig getifaddr en0` prints the IP). If macOS asks whether Python may accept incoming connections, allow it.

The game needs to be served over http; opening `index.html` straight from disk won't load the modules.

### Offline

- **Single file:** `node tools/build_offline.mjs` writes `dist/puckbound-offline.html`, one file of about 95 MB with everything embedded. Double-click it on any computer to play with no server or internet. It isn't kept in git: the Pages workflow (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`) builds it on every push to main and publishes it with the site, at `dist/puckbound-offline.html`.
- **Install on a phone (home screen, offline):** the game is a Progressive Web App with a manifest, icons and a service worker that caches every file the game uses. Phones only allow this from an **https** address. Host the folder on any https static host (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages), open it on the phone, then:
  - Android (Chrome): menu, then *Install app*. The title screen also shows an Install button.
  - iPhone (Safari): Share, then *Add to Home Screen*. On an iPhone or iPad the title screen has a *Play fullscreen* button that walks through it (the Home Screen app keeps a save of its own: Settings › Cloud save carries one across).
  After the first visit it launches fullscreen in landscape and plays with no connection. Progress is saved on the phone.
- After changing any game file, run `node tools/build_pwa.mjs` so the service worker picks up the new version. Pushing to main deploys: the workflow publishes the repository to GitHub Pages with the offline file built fresh.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Gamepad | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Skate | WASD / arrows | Left stick | Drag on the left half |
| Sprint | Shift | RB / LT | SPRINT |
| Shoot (tap = wrist, hold = slapshot) / Check | J or Space | X / RT | SHOOT / CHECK |
| Pass / Switch player | K or Enter | A | PASS / SWITCH |
| Signature skill | U or Q | B / LB | Skill button |

# Hyrule Composite

Minecraft Java × Ocarina of Time. Both games run as native processes: Minecraft
supplies controls, camera, inventory, health and blocks; a patched Ship of
Harkinian supplies Hyrule, its actors and story, and Link's body. Minecraft
shows the combined picture.

Single-player prototype, tested only on x86-64 Arch Linux (Omarchy/Hyprland).
See [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) for where this is going (dedicated server, modpack).

This repository holds bridge source, patches and tooling only. It contains no
Minecraft, ROM, extracted assets, saves or account data. You need your own
Minecraft account and your own supported Ocarina of Time ROM dump.

## Versions

Pinned in [versions.json](versions.json): Minecraft 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.19.5,
JDK 25, Ship of Harkinian 9.3.0.

## Running

```bash
./hyrule start      # start Minecraft
./hyrule status
./hyrule arrange    # put the Minecraft window centre-screen, park Zelda's window
./hyrule restart
./hyrule stop       # Minecraft saves and quits, taking the game engine with it
```

left). It steps through the games that are installed:

- **Minecraft** creates an ordinary Minecraft world.
- **Ocarina of Time** creates a world paired with its own Zelda save. Opening the
  world starts Zelda; leaving it stops Zelda. A new world begins as adult Link in
  Kokiri Forest with everything unlocked; after that it continues from where
  Zelda last saved (it saves automatically).

- **Mario Kart 64 — <track>** (ten tracks) creates a world on that track. You are
  on foot as your Minecraft character and can place blocks and dig into the track
  as in Hyrule. `/spawnkart` asks for a character (1–8) and puts you in that
  character's kart: W accelerate, S brake, A/D steer, Space hop and drift, Shift

# Kestrel

A free, honest FPS optimiser for VALORANT on Windows. Kestrel detects your hardware, finds what's
holding your frames back, and (in later versions) applies reversible tweaks picked for your PC.

> Kestrel is not affiliated with Riot Games. VALORANT is a trademark of Riot Games, Inc.

## Status

Stage 3 (v0.3.0): the Hardware tab. Every part of the PC that Windows reports without a driver, each core's clock
live, and Copy specs for a short summary to paste anywhere. Four new Health Check items look at the graphics card's
PCIe link, Resizable BAR and virtualization, with BIOS-guide steps for your board, and benchmarks record the PCIe
link under load. Kestrel still changes nothing on your PC.

Stage 2 (v0.2.0): the benchmark. A warm-up and 3 runs on a fixed route in VALORANT's Range measure average FPS,
1% and 0.1% lows, stutters and PC latency, and compare every later result with your starting point. Kestrel
changes nothing on your PC; it only saves benchmark results in its own folder.

Stage 1 (v0.1.0): hardware detection, Health Check and BIOS guide.

Next, in this order:

- Stage 4: FiveM, Rainbow Six Siege and Warzone
- Stage 5: the tweak engine, with reversible tweaks picked for your PC
- Stage 6: the Competitive and Extreme tiers
- Stage 7: Lock In
- Stage 8: fixes and the troubleshooter
- Stage 9: the redesign, as v1.0

## Install a test build

1. Open the latest pre-release on the [Releases page](https://github.com/gabryelvs/kestrel/releases).
2. Download `Kestrel_<version>_x64-setup.exe` and run it. Installing over an older version is fine.
3. Test builds aren't signed yet, so Windows may show "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info → Run anyway**.

## What Kestrel will never do

- Read or change VALORANT's memory, or inject anything into it
- Load its own kernel driver
- Touch Riot Vanguard
- Tell you to turn off TPM or Secure Boot
- Permanently disable Defender, UAC or Windows Update
- Download anything while it runs (PresentMon, which measures frames, ships inside the installer)

## Development

Plans live in `docs/superpowers/plans/`. Windows builds run on GitHub Actions.

Before `tauri dev` or `tauri build` on Windows, run `npm run fetch:presentmon` in `app/`: it downloads the pinned PresentMon that ships inside Kestrel, and the build fails without it.

A U2 trivia party game in the style of Jackbox. The TV shows the questions; everyone answers on their phone.

# OpenBRC

OpenBRC is an open source reimplementation of **Barbie Riding Club** (Mattel Media /
Human Code, 1998) for modern Linux, Windows and macOS.

The goal is preservation: the game should look, sound and play as it did in 1998. On top
of that, OpenBRC adds:

- any resolution, aspect ratio and refresh rate, windowed or fullscreen, HiDPI aware;
  the original 640×480 picture is scaled sharply, with optional smooth and CRT filters
- a Vulkan renderer with an automatic OpenGL fallback
- native builds for Linux, Windows 10/11 (with an installer) and macOS 13+ (Intel and Apple Silicon)

> **Status:** in development. See [docs/status.md](docs/status.md) for what works.

## You need the original game

OpenBRC contains **no** Barbie Riding Club content: no pictures, animations, movies,
sounds, music or text. It reads everything from your own copy of the game, which can be
any of:

- the original CD-ROM in a drive (or a copy of its contents)
- a disc image: `.iso`, `.bin`/`.cue` or `.img`
- an installation of the original game (the folder with `Program` and `Resources`); a
  partial installation is combined with the disc, as the original game did

OpenBRC never runs or modifies the original program. It checks that the files are those
of the Barbie Riding Club CD-ROM v1.0 (volume `BRCV1_0`) and refuses to start without
them.

*Barbie* is a trademark of Mattel, Inc. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by
Mattel or Human Code.

## Playing

On first start OpenBRC looks for the game disc, a disc image in your Downloads folder or
an installation, and asks you to choose one if it finds none. You can also pass it on the
command line:

```sh
openbrc --source ~/Downloads/BRCV1_0.ISO       # use this disc image (and remember it)
openbrc --check-source /run/media/$USER/BRCV1_0  # is this usable?
openbrc --setup                                # choose the game disc again
```

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| Alt+Enter, F11 | Fullscreen / windowed |
| F10 | Picture: 4:3 with borders, stretched, or whole-number scale |
| F9 | Filter: sharp, pixelated, smooth, CRT |
| F8 | VSync on/off |
| F12 | Screenshot |

Settings are stored in `openbrc.ini`; saved games, photos and printouts in the data folder:

| Platform | Settings | Saved games, photos, logs |
|---|---|---|
| Linux | `~/.config/openbrc` | `~/.local/share/openbrc` |
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\OpenBRC` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenBRC` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/OpenBRC` | same |
| Portable (Windows ZIP) |

# 🐌 Immortal Snail Chess

Standard chess plus two immortal snails. Every 3 full moves (6 plies) each snail moves one square
toward the enemy king, crushing whatever is on that square. If a snail lands on a king, that king's
side loses.

Everything runs in the browser (static site, no server): the rules engine, a snail-aware search in
a Web Worker, and Stockfish 18 (lite, single-threaded WASM, ~7 MB) in another worker.

## Quick start

```bash
npm install          # also copies Stockfish into public/stockfish/
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173
npm test             # engine + bot trap suites (pure TS search)
STOCKFISH=1 npm test # also run the trap suites through Stockfish + snail rescoring
npm run selfplay -- --games 20             # Medium vs Hard self-play report
npm run build && npm run preview           # production build
npx tsx scripts/smoke.ts                   # browser smoke test against preview (Chromium)
```

Deploy: `dist/` is a static site (Cloudflare Pages / Vercel). `public/_redirects` gives Pages its
SPA fallback.

## Rules as implemented

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Start | White snail **a4** (hunts the Black king), Black snail **h5** (hunts the White king). |
| Timing | A tick fires after plies 6, 12, 18… (after Black's 3rd, 6th… move). White's snail resolves first. |
| Step | `(sign(dFile), sign(dRank))` toward the target king, i.e. one Chebyshev step (diagonal when both axes differ). |
| Clash | If the other snail is on that square, the snail takes another neighbouring square that still strictly shortens its Chebyshev distance (nearest to the king first), or waits. |
| Crush | Any piece on the landing square is removed, of either colour. A crushed king loses immediately (`snail_win_white` / `snail_win_black` name the winner). If White's snail crushes a king, Black's snail does not move that tick. |
| Walls | Nothing may land on a snail. Sliders, pawn double pushes and castling can't pass through one; knights can jump over. Snails also block lines of attack, so they block checks and pins. |
| Snail exposes a king | If a snail stepping away opens a line so that the side to move could capture the enemy king, the side to move wins (reported as `checkmate`). |
| Draws | Stalemate, 50-move rule, insufficient material, threefold repetition (positions include snail squares and the tick phase). |

# Send It

Golf, but riskier. Send It is a phone game that sits on top of a normal round of golf with friends.

Before each hole, every player picks **Safe**, **Bold** or **Insane** and draws a random challenge card from that pile. Everyone gets a different card. You play the hole for real, then enter your real strokes and whether you completed the card.

| Level  | Completed  | Failed     |
| ------ | ---------- | ---------- |
| Safe   | −2 strokes | +1 stroke  |
| Bold   | −4 strokes | +2 strokes |
| Insane | −6 strokes | +3 strokes |

Each hole: real strokes, minus or plus the card, scored over or under par like golf. Lowest total wins. Real strokes are always kept separately, and the app never passes a game score off as a real golf score.

Twists: the last 3 holes of a 6+ hole round count double, last place gets one free shot a round, everyone gets one redraw, and cards judged by eye go to a group vote online.

Everyone plays on their own phone. Starting a game gets a 5-letter code straight away, with a share link (`/j/CODE`) and a QR code. A turn-based sci-fi RPG in the spirit of classic browser RPGs like AdventureQuest, rendered with three.js. The setting is an original, Star Trek-inspired one: you serve aboard the exploration vessel *Meridian*.

The repository is still called `questforge`; the in-game title is set in `src/ui/ui.ts` (`GAME_TITLE`) and `public/index.html`.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173 with live reload

| `npm run dev` | Dev server (esbuild), rebuilds and reloads on change |

NestJS + grammY + PostgreSQL. Баланс пополняется Telegram Stars (XTR). Подарки — этап 2.

## Игры
| Игра | Механика |
|---|---|
| 🚀 Ракета | Общие раунды для всех: 5 секунд приёма ставок → полёт → краш → пауза → следующий раунд (таймлайн считает сервер, `src/games/engines/rocket-schedule.ts`, точка краша выводится из `ROCKET_SECRET` и открывается только после краша). Нужно успеть «Забрать» до краша; есть авто-вывод (работает и если игрок закрыл приложение). Рядом ставят боты (одинаковые у всех, зависят от номера раунда): ✓ — забрал, ⏳ — ждёт, ✕ — проиграл. |
| 💣 Мины | Поле 5×5, 3–24 мины, каждая открытая клетка повышает икс; RTP 85% (`MINES_EDGE`), поэтому звёзды собирать сложнее, чем в остальных играх. |
| 🏗 Башня | Игра на мастерство: домик раскачивается на верёвке, игрок тапает по экрану, когда он над зелёной зоной на крыше башни. Качание и проверку тапа считает сервер (`src/games/engines/tower.ts`). С высотой качание быстрее, а зелёная зона уже; допуск по времени ±40 мс. Попал — домик встаёт (почти по центру зоны), промахнулся — падает. Иксы: x2 на 5-м этаже (розово-белый домик), x4.97 на 10-м, дальше «космос» до ≈x12.9. |
| 🕊 Чайка | Чайка летит над 3 детьми и хватает одного; угадай, кого она **не** заберёт. 12 шагов, икс растёт с каждым. |

RTP игр 92% (`HOUSE_EDGE`; Мины — 85%, `MINES_EDGE`; Башня — на мастерство) (см. `src/games/engines/types.ts`); проверяется симуляцией в `test/engines.spec.ts`.
Исход каждого раунда определяется сидом до первого хода, а лимит выплаты (`MAX_PAYOUT`) ограничивает риск.

## Честность (provably fair)
Перед раундом игрок видит `sha256(serverSeed)`, после — сам `serverSeed`. Все случайные числа:
`HMAC_SHA256(serverSeed, clientSeed:nonce:i)` (`src/fair/fair.ts`) — любой раунд можно переиграть.

## Запуск
```bash
cp .env.example .env        # BOT_TOKEN, WEBAPP_URL, ADMIN_IDS, ROCKET_SECRET, DATABASE_URL ...
docker compose up -d --build   # база + всё казино (API, бот, Mini App) на :3000
npm install && npm run setup:bot   # проверка токена и Stars-платежей, команды бота, кнопка Mini App
npm test
```
Без Docker: `docker compose up -d db && npm install && npm run build && npm start`.

### Подключение настоящего пополнения Stars (чек-лист)
1. @BotFather → `/newbot` → токен в `BOT_TOKEN`. Для Stars (XTR) платёжный провайдер не нужен.
2. Сервер с публичным **HTTPS** (VPS + Caddy/nginx, Render, Fly.io…) на порт 3000; адрес — в `WEBAPP_URL`.
3. @BotFather → `/mybots` → ваш бот →

# RShop

**Website and download: https://animatrixex.github.io/RShop/**

**A game store for Android handhelds.** Browse a catalogue, download, install and manage games, with a console-style interface built for controllers.

RShop is **only a store and a download/install manager**. It does not launch games (that stays with your frontend or emulators) and it ships **no catalogue**: you add sources whose content you have the right to download (homebrew, your own creations, freely licensed content, your own server…).

Made for Retroid, Ayn, Anbernic and similar devices (16:9, gamepad); works on any Android 13+ phone or tablet.

| Home | Game page |

| **Catalogue sources** | **Appearance** |

# THE NIGHT MANAGER

A multiplayer survival-horror / social-deduction / life-sim Roblox game by **Nexus Hollow Studios** (group owner: Swag_Boy435 / V1RTU4L).

The code lives here as plain Luau files. **Rojo** syncs them into Roblox Studio, **Lune** tests the game logic on any computer, and a GitHub Action can publish the game to Roblox.

```
src/shared   code both sides use (ReplicatedStorage.Shared)   <- put testable logic here
src/server   server scripts (ServerScriptService.Server)
src/client   client scripts (StarterPlayerScripts.Client)
tests        checks that run without Roblox:  lune run tests/run
brand        logo and store art
art          Blender scripts, models, renders (docs/ART.md)
docs         HANDOFF, GAMEPLAY, MAP, ART, PLAYTEST, IDEAS, ROADMAP, marketing
```

## What the game is

Four to ten staff are locked in a hotel on the night shift. **The Night Manager** hunts them across three floors. The **crew** finish tasks, **one of them is a saboteur** helping him. Run (loud), light your flashlight (he notices), hide in lockers and wardrobes (he searches), report bodies, ring the lobby bell, vote someone out. More in `docs/GAMEPLAY.md`.

# Ultime Player — Prends le contrôle de ta carrière

Mobile-first career sim built with Next.js 14 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind, Framer Motion, Lucide and Zustand (LocalStorage persistence).

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000  (best viewed at phone width)
npm run build && npm start
```

## Structure
- `app/` — routes: `/` title, `/create` FTUE, `(game)/` home · match · calendar · transfers · profile
- `components/match/` — locker-room talk, live ticker + momentum, clutch sheet, **8-zone `GoalTarget`**, shootout, press zone, summary
- `lib/engine/` — pure, testable logic: `match`, `kick` (keeper dive), `shootout`, `season`, `transfers`, `player`
- `lib/data/` — mock data: clubs, nationalities, speeches, press questions, clutch deck
- `lib/store.ts` — Zustand store persisted to LocalStorage (`fcs-save-v1`)

## Lives, shop and the App Store

- **Lives** regenerate one every 3 minutes (up to 5). A match costs one life.
- **Money** (earned every match) buys lasting upgrades in `/shop`: personal coach (more performance XP),
  nutritionist (less fatigue), media advisor (fewer scandals), agent (better contracts) and a yearly charity gala.
  Attributes themselves only grow through performance on the pitch — never through purchases.
- **Unlimited-lives passes** (€3.99 for 3 h, €4.99 for 24 h; they stack) go through `lib/payments.ts`.
  - In development (or with `NEXT_PUBLIC_IAP_TEST=1`) a test provider grants lives instantly, without any payment.
  - In production on the web the packs are disabled. The native iOS shell (e.g. Capacitor + RevenueCat/StoreKit)
    must call `registerPaymentProvider({ name: 'storekit', isReal: true, purchase })` at start-up.
  - Apple requires In-App Purchase for digital consumables like these, takes a commission (15–30 %),
    and needs a privacy policy URL, an age rating and the price tiers configured in App Store Connect.
- Everything runs in the browser (static pages + `localStorage`), so hosting costs no server CPU.

## iPhone app

The game also ships as an iPhone app (Capacitor + Xcode, with in-app purchases). See [IOS.md](IOS.md): `npm run ios`.

# Apex Drive - Unity edition

A port of the Three.js "Apex Drive" first-person F1 game to Unity. Everything (track meshes, cars, HUD,
menu, weather) is generated in code, so there is nothing to wire up in the editor.

## Run it
1. Install Unity **2022.3 LTS** (newer versions open it too and will offer to upgrade).
2. Unity Hub -> Add -> select this `apex-drive-unity` folder -> open it. Use the built-in render
   pipeline (this project has no URP/HDRP package; if you drop the scripts into a URP project the
   materials fall back to the URP Lit shader automatically).
3. Open any scene (or leave the default empty one) and press **Play**. `Bootstrap` creates the game
   at startup via `RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod`.
4. If your project's Active Input Handling is "Input System Package (New)", switch it to
   "Input Manager (Old)" or "Both" under Project Settings > Player (the scripts use `UnityEngine.Input`).

## Controls
W / Up throttle, S / Down brake, A D / Left Right steer, Q DRS (in the DRS zone), E engine mode,
V cockpit / chase camera, R recover to centre line, P or Esc pause, 1 - 5 choose tires during a pit stop (soft, medium, hard, inter, wet), Y / N answer the pit-wall radio calls.
B = box this lap (lane assist + stops you in the box), Shift = ERS overtake button (spends the battery), Z / X / C = look left / right / behind.
Replay (from the results screen): Space pause, Left/Right scrub, 1 drone, 2 trackside, 3 chase, 4 next car, F hide UI, Enter photo, Esc exit.

## What's ported
- The three circuits (Harborline, Desert Straight, Sprint Alley; Silverstone was removed from the Unity version) with the same control points,
  elevation profiles and per-track rain / fog odds; same Catmull-Rom spline, arc-length spacing, wall
  clearance and curvature maths (`TrackModel.cs`).
- Road, curbs, guard rails, gravel, terrain skirt, grandstands, trees, hills, start/finish gantry.
- Pit lane as a real separate road, with its own wall between lane and track, pit crew, sign and box
  marking. Pit stops are opt-in: you must steer into the lane (never a forced magnet).
- Car physics from `updatePlayer()`: drag-limited acceleration, tire wear + compounds, wing / gear / brake
  setup, corner limit, crest launch + gravity, wall damage, track limits + penalties, slipstream, DRS.
- AI rivals with look-ahead braking, mistakes, tire wear and pit stops.
- Weather (rain with wet-track grip loss, fog), sector times with deltas vs your best, lap timing, HUD,
  minimap, garage wi

# Chair Run × Mutual Mimu

A game and landing page by **MIMU ON APE**, built by Bert Baccaratt, for the TMF Pass Mimu giveaway. It is independent and not affiliated with THE MUTUAL FUN project (see the NDA screen and the Terms of Service on the site).

A phone lies on a wood desk, and the phone is the game: Chair Run (a pseudo-3D runner), Mutual Mimu (stake, vote and a closing bell every 4h 20m), Leaderboards, Badges, Top 5, Alarm, Messages, Phone, Camera and Settings.

## Run the site locally

It is a static site: `index.html`, `admin.html` and `assets/`. Serve the folder with any static server, then open http://localhost:8765/ :

```
npx serve -l 8765 .
```

Local-only helpers: `?gate=ok` fakes a Glyph sign-in (only on `localhost`), and `?api=http://localhost:8787` points the game at a local Worker (only on `localhost`).

## What is where

- `index.html`: the whole game and landing page (HTML, CSS, JS)
- `admin.html`: the admin page (password checked by the server; visitor flip clock, top lists, review queue, texts, players, live runs)
- `assets/`: images, `sim.js` (the shared game core), `glyph-connect.js` (the Glyph bundle, loaded only when Chair Run opens)

- `backend/`: Cloudflare Worker + D1 database (API at https://mimu-mutual-api.mutualmimu.workers.dev), `schema.sql`, and the test scripts
- `tools/`: one-off build and patch scripts (not needed to run the site)

## How the game works with the server

- **Sign in:** the wallet signs a free plain-English message that names this site. The server checks the signature, the origin and the holdings (a wallet must hold a Mimu On Ape; a wallet holding a TMF Pass or a Dengs can't play). The bridge refuses to sign anything else.

# Kriegsspiel

A slow, long-running wargame played against a continuous game clock (1:1, 4:1, 12:1 or any ratio), based on the classic Prussian *Kriegsspiel* (von Reisswitz, 1824), with an **LLM umpire** on the server.

You never move pieces. You write orders. Subordinates interpret them, couriers carry them (or don't), and the umpire tells each side only what its commander would plausibly know.

## Idea in one paragraph

A deterministic engine owns the world: terrain, movement, line of sight, combat, dice. An LLM owns language: it turns free-text orders into structured intents, makes bounded judgment calls where the rules are silent (the umpire's discretion in "free Kriegsspiel"), and narrates fog-filtered reports for each player. The model never changes state directly, and everything it does is logged and replayable.

## Docs

- [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md): decision log and open questions (start here)
- [docs/research.md](docs/research.md): history of Kriegsspiel, rigid vs free rules, related LLM wargaming work, sources
- [docs/design.md](docs/design.md): pillars, feature ideas, hybrid adjudication model, trust risks
- [docs/gameplay.md](docs/gameplay.md): how Kriegsspiel is played, the continuous game clock, pacing, pausing, and collaborative roles
- [docs/hq-interface.md](docs/hq-interface.md): the general's-HQ desk: historical map table, in-tray of dispatches, orders desk, staff
- [docs/hq-getting-started.md](docs/hq-getting-started.md): current HQ features, user instructions and hands-on validation checklist
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): server/engine/umpire design, tech choices, testing
- [docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md): milestones and what is done

## Current state

Epic 1 (the playable vertical slice) is done: you can start a game, write orders, wait for couriers and reports, and play "Hold the Bridge" to a win or loss in a browser, and the same game replays identically from its log. Since then the project has gained an Angular 22 client over a Three.js map table (with the desk: in-tray, orders, order of battle, journal, staff conference), accounts, guest play and a lobby, pause and ratio voting, notifications, an LLM umpire that runs on Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible or local Ollama providers (the rule-based parser remains the fallback), an LLM or scripted opposing commander, a post-game umpire's window, and a visual design system. See [docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md) for what is done and what is next.

# QuestCraft for NeoForge

A port of [QuestCraft](https://github.com/QuestCraftPlusPlus/QuestCraft) (Minecraft: Java Edition in VR on Meta Quest and other standalone headsets) from the **Fabric** mod loader to **NeoForge**. The launcher has a **loader toggle** between **Fabric**, **NeoForge**, **Quilt**, **Forge**, **Vanilla** (1.12.2 in VR) and **Risugami** (Risugami's ModLoader, alpha to 1.6.2), and NeoForge is the default.

QuestCraft itself is not a mod. | [`unity-wrapper/`](unity-wrapper) | [QCXR-XR-Wrapper](https://github.com/QuestCraftPlusPlus/QCXR-XR-Wrapper), `master` | Creates NeoForge instances, Mod Manager searches/validates mods for the instance's loader |

# Poké Train

Track Pokédex progress and a trained competitive roster across Pokémon games. The first game module is **Pokémon Violet**.

- **Pokédex grid** per regional dex with click, shift-click range and drag-to-paint toggling. Each game also has its own **National Dex** tab: the same caught list as its regional dexes, with a badge on Pokémon you caught in your other games.
- **Spreadsheet importer** (.csv / .xlsx) with a column-mapping step. Reads Spanish or English names and tolerates typos.
- **Trained roster**: small cards with paging on the left, and everything about the selected Pokémon on the right, editable in place. Every nature, ability, item, EV spread and move is a checklist item: orange while pending, green when done.
- **Spanish and English.** The ES/EN switch in the header changes the whole app: menus, buttons, messages and Pokémon, move, item and ability names. AI answers are written in the language selected when you ask. A saved AI answer is never translated: switching language keeps it, and the card says which language it is in until you re-run it in the new one (a copy you already have in that language is reused for free).
- **Pokémon details.** Click any Pokédex card for its information from PokéAPI: description, stats, abilities, egg groups, gender, size, evolution line and where it sits in the game's Pokédexes. Marking uses the **Catch** button on the card (shift-click fills a range).
- **Version exclusives.** For paired games (Scarlet/Violet) the **Exclusives** tab is a small Pokédex of what only your version has and what only the other version has, with a "Scarlet only" / "Violet only" tag on Pokédex cards. # Taoob Arcade

ห้องเกมรวม A-Math, Sudoku, เกม 24, หมากรุก, หมากฮอส พร้อมบัญชีผู้เล่น (ชื่อผู้ใช้ + รหัสผ่าน) และตารางอันดับรายคน
ใช้ GitHub Pages โฮสต์หน้าเว็บ และ Supabase เก็บบัญชี/อันดับ (รหัสผ่านถูกแฮชโดย Supabase Auth ไม่ได้เก็บเป็นข้อความธรรมดา)

## ตั้งค่า (ทำครั้งเดียว)

### 1) สร้างตารางใน Supabase (ถ้าเคยรันแล้ว ให้รันไฟล์ใหม่อีกครั้ง เพื่อเพิ่มหมากรุก/หมากฮอส รันซ้ำได้ปลอดภัย)
Supabase Dashboard → **SQL Editor** → New query → วางทั้งไฟล์ `schema.sql` → **Run**

### 2) ปิดการยืนยันอีเมล
Supabase Dashboard → **Authentication → Sign In / Providers → Email** → ปิด **Confirm email** → Save
(ระบบนี้ใช้ชื่อผู้ใช้ ไม่มีอีเมลจริง จึงยืนยันอีเมลไม่ได้)

### 3) อัปโหลดขึ้น GitHub
สร้าง repo (เช่นชื่อ `arcade`) แล้วอัปโหลดทุกไฟล์ในโฟลเดอร์นี้ไว้ที่ราก:
```
index.html  platform.js  schema.sql  icons/  amath/  sudoku/  game24/  chess/  checkers/  .nojekyll
```
Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → `main` / `(root)` แล้วเปิด `https://<ชื่อ GitHub>.github.io/arcade/`

## หมายเหตุ
- ชื่อผู้ใช้ใช้ได้ a-z 0-9 และ _ ยาว 3–16 ตัว (ไม่สนตัวพิมพ์ใหญ่เล็ก) รหัสผ่านต้องมี 6 ตัวขึ้นไป (เบราว์เซอร์แปลงเป็นรหัสยาวด้วย SHA-256 ก่อนส่ง)
- **ลืมรหัสผ่าน:** กด "ลืมรหัสผ่าน? รีเซตรหัสผ่าน" ในหน้าเข้าสู่ระบบ ใส่ชื่อผู้ใช้ให้ตรง แล้วตั้งรหัสผ่านใหม่ + ยืนยัน (ไม่ใช้อีเมลหรือรหัสเดิม) ข้อควรรู้: ใครรู้ชื่อผู้ใช้ก็รีเซตรหัสของชื่อนั้นได้ จึงเหมาะกับกลุ่มเพื่อนเล่นกันเอง
- **ต้องรัน `schema.sql` ใหม่อีกรอบ** ใน Supabase SQL Editor เพื่อเพิ่มฟังก์ชันรีเซตรหัสผ่าน (รันซ้ำได้ ข้อมูลเดิมไม่หาย)
- ยังไม่ล็อกอินก็เล่นได้ แต่ผลจะไม่ถูกบันทึก
- ผลถูกส่งจากฝั่งเบราว์เซอร์ ผู้เล่นที่มีความรู้เทคนิคอาจแก้ตัวเลขได้ (ฟังก์ชันจำกัดแต้มต่อครั้งไม่เกิน 20) เหมาะกับการเล่นระหว่างเพื่อน
- แต้มรวม: ชนะระดับง่าย/กลาง/ยาก/โหด ได้ 1/2/4/8 (A-Math สู้ AI 2/4/8) ชนะเพื่อน 5 แต้ม ถ้าใช้ใบ้ไม่ได้แต้มและไม่นับเวลา
- ค่าเชื่อมต่อ Supabase อยู่บนสุดของ `platform.js` (ใช้ publishable key เท่านั้น ห้ามใส่ service_role key)

# lizpop.art

Liz Karcewski's website. Hosted free on GitHub Pages. The domain is registered at WordPress.com.

## Editing the site (no code needed)

Go to **https://lizpop.art/admin/** and sign in.

| Section | What it controls |
|---|---|
| Quotes | The daily quote on the home page. Add, edit, reorder, or turn one off with "Show on site." |
| Prints | The print wall. Each print links to its Etsy listing. |
| Brand portfolio | Projects at lizpop.art/portfolio. Turn on "Feature on home page" for up to 3. |
| Page text and links | Home page text, book details and buy links, the book signing, brand stats, About, social links. |

Every save becomes a commit in this repo, so nothing is ever truly lost. Changes go live in about 1 to 2 minutes.

### Signing in

Each person needs a GitHub account with access to this repo:

1. Mark adds Liz under **Settings > Collaborators** in the repo.
2. On the admin login screen, click **Sign In with Token**. It links to GitHub with the right settings filled in.
3. If making the token by hand, use a **fine-grained token**, limited to only the `lizpop-site` repo, with **Contents: Read and write**.
4. Paste the token once. The browser remembers it. Don't share tokens; each person makes their own.

### Images

- Uploads are automatically resized and converted to WebP so the site stays fast.
- Always fill in the image description. It's what screen readers read aloud.
- Print images currently link to Etsy's photos. If one ever breaks, upload the image directly instead.

### Videos

Don't upload video files to the repo; GitHub isn't built for large files.

- YouTube, YouTube Shorts, and Vimeo links play right on the site.
- Instagram and TikTok links open in a new tab (their embeds slow pages down and track visitors).
- For each video, upload a cover image (a screenshot from the video works).

## Automatic Etsy sync

Every morning (about 6:23am Eastern) GitHub pulls Liz's active Etsy listings:
- New listings are added to the top of the Prints list and shown on the site.
- Listings that are no longer on Etsy are removed.
- Edits made in the admin panel (titles, order, hiding) are kept.
- The home page shows the first 12 shown prints (change this under Page text and links > Shop).

To run it right away: repo **Actions** tab > **Sync and deploy** > **Run workflow**.

It needs two repo secrets (**Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions**): `ETSY_API_KEY` and `ETSY_SHARED_SECRET`, from Liz's app at etsy.com/developers/your-apps. Witho

# Futkrill

A football trivia game with a shared free daily, 30-second rounds, rarity scoring, pixel-art reveals and optional Unlimited access.

- `web/`: Next.js application, Stripe one-time purchases, Supabase email verification and database migrations.
- `pipeline/`: Python football-data preparation and prompt generation.
- `art/`: Artwork generation source.

## Development

Use Node.js 24 or newer. From a fresh checkout:

```sh
cd web
npm ci
cp .env.example .env.development.local
npm run dev -- --port 3100
```

Fill local environment values from your own sandbox configuration. Never commit credentials. The daily remains available without billing configuration. See [web setup](web/README.md) for Stripe, Supabase and email settings.

## Working with Claude Code and Codex

Use a separate clone or Git worktree for each coding agent. Start each change from the latest `main` on a separate branch, such as `claude/gameplay` or `codex/billing`. Open pull requests and review changes before merging. Do not have two agents edit the same checkout or push over each other's branch.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/emrekapancibuilds/futbol-krillion.git
cd futbol-krillion
git switch -c claude/gameplay
```

The repository contains source and public game data only. Runtime credentials, local billing records, database dumps and internal handoff reports stay outside Git. A new clone needs its own ignored environment file.

## Current behavior

This version uses a $4.99 USD one-time Stripe purchase. Supabase verifies the checkout email when restoring a purchase; it creates a passwordless Auth identity only when that flow is requested. Browser progress stays local. Stripe payment status and server-side ownership determine paid access.

The public repository is not an automatic production deployment. Local sandbox verification has covered Checkout, paid access, receipts, refunds and webhook replay. Supabase's default email sender is suitable only for project-team testing; configure custom SMTP before emailing real customers or branding emails.

## Parallel work branches

- `main`: one-time $4.99 Unlimited purchase with Supabase verified-email restoration.
- `codex/one-time-unlimited`: conversion from the earlier monthly test implementation.
- `claude/one-time-unlock`: preserved historical Claude experiment. Its email-only restoration is not secure; do not merge its backend into the app.

# PotatoBrawl

A 1v1 potato platform fighter that runs in the browser. Anyone with the link can play,
with no account and no install. One small Node.js process serves the page and relays
online matches.

## What is in here

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `public/index.html` | The game: menus, eight potato fighters, CPU ranked ladder, tournament, practice, online play |
| `server.js` | Serves the page, relays online matches over WebSocket (`/ws`), keeps itself awake |
| `package.json` | One dependency: `ws` (pinned to 8.21.3) |
| `render.yaml` | Render setup: free web service in Frankfurt |
| `potatobrawl.service` | For running on your own Linux server instead (systemd) |

## Put it online on Render (free)

1. **Put this folder on GitHub.** Create a new repository (private is fine), then use
   *Add file → Upload files* and drag in everything from this folder, so `render.yaml`
   sits at the top level of the repository. Commit.
2. **Create the service.** In the Render dashboard choose *New → Blueprint*, connect your
   GitHub account, pick the repository and confirm. Render reads `render.yaml` and creates
   a free web service called `potatobrawl` in Frankfurt.
3. **Wait for the first deploy** (a minute or two). Your game is then at
   `https://potatobrawl.onrender.com`, or a similar name if that one is taken. That link is
   what you send to friends.
4. **Check it's awake.** Open `https://<your-service>.onrender.com/health`. A few minutes
   after a deploy it shows the time of the last keep-alive ping.

To update the game later, replace `public/index.html` in the repository. Render redeploys
on its own after each commit.

### Graphics

The fighters and stage are drawn in 2D on a canvas. Graphics never affect online play: both
browsers simulate the same game regardless of what each one draws.

### Staying awake for free

Render stops a free web service after 15 minutes without incoming traffic, and the first
visit after that takes about a minute to load. `server.js` prevents this on its own: every
4 minutes it requests its own public address (`RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL`, which Render sets),
and that request counts as incoming traffic. You don't need UptimeRobot or another outside
pinger. If you ever want one anyway, point it at `/health`; any interval under 15 minutes
works.

# Zombie Horde Survivors

A browser-based 3D squad shooter: command a small squad of soldiers and a drone against waves of zombies, skeletons, aliens, hounds, brutes and giant worms. Play it **hands-on** (direct control of one soldier, in top-down, third-person or first-person view) or **from above** (RTS mode: select units and give orders).

Built with Three.js + Vite + TypeScript. No backend: it runs in the browser.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # dev server (http://localhost:5173)
npm run build    # static files in dist/
npm test         # unit tests

You start in **direct control** of one soldier, with the rest of the squad following you and shooting on their own. Press **Y** to switch to **RTS mode**, select units, send them anywhere on the map, then press **Y** again to take direct control of one of them.

readme:
# Idle Casino

**Play now:** https://giider.github.io/idle-casino/  
**Download the single-file build:** https://github.com/GIider/idle-casino/releases/tag/latest (`idle-casino.html`, runs offline)

Every push to `main` runs the tests, builds a self-contained HTML file and publishes it as the `latest` release and to GitHub Pages.

A single-player browser idle game. Every table plays itself the moment it opens; you spend each table's winnings on speed, bigger bets and odds-tilting upgrades, and prestige tables to raise their stakes. Tables are chained: each one stakes the previous table's currency and pays its winnings in its own, so every currency is either spent on its own table's upgrades or fed downstream as stakes.

## Tables
| Table | Pays out in | Stakes / unlock (previous table's currency) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Coin Flip | 🪙 Pennies | free | slight player edge, the first rung of the ladder |
| Slots | 🎟️ Tokens | 1,500 Pennies | weighted reels, three-of-a-kind jackpots |
| Roulette | 🔶 Plaques | 7,500 Tokens | starts on red; buy the dozen and number 17 bets to spread each stake across them |
| Blackjack | ♠️ Markers | 37,500 Plaques | naturals pay 3:2, upgrades bend the deck |

## Mechanics
- **Chained wallets**: Coin Flip stakes and wins its own Pennies. Every later table *stakes the previous table's currency* (each unit of bet costs 0.3 of it, 0.1 at Blackjack) and pays its winnings into its own wallet; upgrades are bought with that own wallet, and unlocking the next table costs it. A per-table *Stakes* slider (default 30%) caps how much of the upstream wallet the table may draw on, so you choose between feeding a table and upgrading the one before it. Coin Flip keeps a bankroll of 50 minimum bets that downstream tables can't touch. A table with nothing to stake is simply idle, never comped; only Coin Flip is bailed out. Every table has a small built-in winnings bonus so it can climb on its own before you buy anything.
- **Cross-table bonus**: every prestige level of a table gives the next table in the chain +4% winnings, so earlier tables stay worth playing and prestiging.
- **Endless upgrades**: *High Roller Perks* doesn't max out at level 20; every further level compounds (×1.25 winnings and max payout) for a steeper price (×1.38 per level), so prestige targets stay reachable indefinitely.
- **Lucky Charm**: a chance to re-roll a losing round. **High Roller Perks**: bigger winnings. **Hot Streak**: each win in a row adds winning

# Soundlings

A phonics reading game for five-year-olds, built on the Australian synthetic phonics sequence.

A child completes a level when they can **prove they can read the words** — cold, a day later, unaided — not when they have played a fixed number of games.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
cd "apps/game" && npm run web
```

Then open <http://localhost:8081>.

On a real iPad — which is the version that counts for a children's app — install **Expo Go** from the App Store, run `npx expo start` from `apps/game`, and scan the QR code. No Xcode needed.

```bash
npm test          # 1787 tests
npm run typecheck
```

## What's here

| Package | What it does |
|---|---|
| `packages/curriculum` | Teaching content as pure data: graphemes, words, levels, creatures. Zero dependencies. |
| `packages/engine` | The adaptive engine — mastery model, session builder, frustration guard, distractor picker, simulation harness. Pure TypeScript, no React, no clock, no RNG. |
| `packages/api` | The sync layer over Supabase. `rebuild.ts` and `syncQueue.ts` are pure and decide whether a child's history survives; the rest moves data. |
| `packages/ui` | Soft Paper design tokens. |
| `packages/audio` | Audio-key manifest and a queue that never overlaps speech. |
| `apps/game` | Expo app: profiles, island home, four mini-games, quest runner. |

`curriculum` and `engine` are deliberately pure so the adaptive logic — the part of this product that actually differentiates it — can be tested adversarially. It needed to be: simulation found a version of this engine where Level 1 **could not be completed at all**, while every unit test passed.

PS1 and PS2 in full, and an honest PS3 card. (Formerly the *PS2 Boot Inspection Tool*.) ![The opening, built from the play history on a memory card](docs/opening.png) Nothing from Sony ships with the app. You bring a BIOS image, a PCSX2 memory card and, if you want the disc phase, a disc image; the tool reads them at run time. ## What you can inspect ### Memory card data, as towers The towers in the PS2 boot screen are a picture of the console's play history: every title on the card owns six slots in a 14×9 grid, a title's first launch plants a tower, and more towers grow with the number of launches. The tool reads `B?DATA-SYSTEM/history` straight from a PCSX2 card image or folder card and builds the skyline from it, so two cards give two different boot screens, side by side if you like. # Exploderous

A Bomberman-clone in Rust with a focus on correctness through different testing techniques.

## Development

Install [rustup](https://rustup.rs/). Cargo commands automatically provision the Rust version, `rustfmt`, and `clippy` pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`, both locally and in CI:

```sh
cargo run -p exploderous-tui --locked
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --all-targets --locked
```

The root is a virtual workspace. The separate movement playground is `crates/tui` (package `exploderous-tui`) and requires a terminal with Kitty keyboard-protocol support. Each run overwrites `app.log` with all terminal events, per-tick movement inputs and positions, and catch-up/error records; pasted contents are redacted. The headless movement core lives in `crates/core` (package `exploderous-core`); root-level check commands cover all workspace members. CI runs formatting, Clippy (warnings fail), and tests on pushes and pull requests.

## Current route

Start with a headless game core and basic TUI; expand gameplay and local competitive modes incrementally. Add frontend and networking crates under `crates/` when their delivery slices begin, keeping the core independent of them. Graphics, networking, and browser support will be evaluated as the project develops.

- [Game-state and simulation design](docs/design/game-state.md)

# ArcadeForge AI — Design, Compile, and Play Retro Arcade Games

**ArcadeForge AI** is a mobile-first retro arcade creation studio powered by **GPT-6 Astra**. Users collaborate with AI through an iterative design conversation or mobile QR scan wizard to conceive, balance, compile, and instantly play custom 2D arcade games.

---

## Key Features

### 🕹️ Multi-Genre Arcade Engine
* **Beat 'Em Up:** Classic brawler mechanics (inspired by The Simpsons & TMNT arcade classics) with combo attacks, crowd control, and health pick-ups.
* **Dungeon Crawler & Rogue-Like:** Grid-based and real-time procedurally inspired labyrinths with enemy mobs and loot.
* **Side-Scrolling Platformer:** Precision jumps, hazards, and scrolling backgrounds.
* **Retro Shmup / Space Shooter:** Wave-based bullet patterns and power-ups.
* **Retro Board & Turn-Based Games:** Classic tabletop strategy digitized into retro pixel art.

### 📱 Mobile-First Design & QR Onboarding
* **Scan to Design:** Scan the on-screen QR code from any smartphone camera to open the mobile game design wizard.
* **Virtual Arcade Controls:** Touch-optimized on-screen directional pad and responsive Action [A] / Attack [B] buttons with haptic feedback.
* **Chiptune Audio Synthesizer:** Real-time Web Audio 8-bit sound effects and retro jingles.

### 🧠 Powered by GPT-6 Astra
* **Iterative Dialogue Studio:** Converse with GPT-6 Astra to tweak enemy speeds, add character moves, change pixel themes, and balance difficulty.
* **Dual Runtime:** Runs instantly in browser Canvas and exports complete standalone Python Pygame source code (`game.py`) for desktop execution.

readme:
# Dael's Phone

A pretend phone for a toddler. Everything is local: no network, no real calls, no ads.

## What's inside

- **Phone**: a dial pad that speaks each digit. Dialing any number "connects" to a silly animal or vehicle.
- **Family**: tap Mom, Dad, or anyone else to start a pretend video call that plays a clip you recorded.
  The front camera shows the child's own face in the corner like a real call.
- **Surprise incoming calls**: every few minutes someone from the family "calls".
- **Animals, Piano, Paint, Peekaboo** games.
- **Parent settings**: hold the top-right corner of the home screen for 3 seconds, then answer a
  multiplication question. From there you add photos, record or pick videos, toggle kiosk mode,
  and exit the app.

## Kiosk mode

With kiosk mode on, the app pins itself (Android screen pinning) on every resume so the Home and
Back gestures cannot leave it. Android shows a one-time confirmation dialog the first time.
Use "Unpin and exit app" in parent settings to leave. The app also registers as a HOME launcher,
so on a dedicated old phone you can make it the default home screen.

## Voices and icons

Spoken phrases are pre-generated natural voice clips in `app/src/main/res/raw`, made with the
[Kokoro](https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro) neural TTS by `tools/gen_voices.py`. Re-run it with
`--child <name>` to regenerate them for your own child. Phrases without a clip (for example a
family member with an unusual name) fall back to the phone's text-to-speech engine.
Icons are drawn as vector drawables by `tools/gen_icons.py`.

## Making it impossible to unpin (dedicated phone only)

Screen pinning can be escaped by holding Back and Recents. On a spare phone with no Google
account signed in, make the app the device owner once over ADB and lock task mode becomes
unescapable until you remove it:

```
adb shell dpm set-device-owner me.tewodros.dael/.DaelAdmin
adb shell dpm remove-active-admin me.tewodros.dael/.DaelAdmin   # to undo
```

This is not possible on a phone that already has accounts, which is why it is not the default.

## Build

Needs JDK 17+ and the Android SDK (`local.properties` points at `~/Android/Sdk`).

```
./gradlew installDebug      # build and install on a connected phone
```

An HTML5 first-person parkour game, deployed on Cloudflare Pages and embedded (iframe) into another website.

A seaside carnival boardwalk where time only moves when you do. The hot dog vendors have had enough:
they wind up (a mustard telegraph line), hurl hot dogs, and the hot dogs hang in the air while you stand still.
Run, jump, slide, mantle and wall-run down the pier; dodge the dogs, shove vendors at arm's reach,
or let them pelt each other. Every hot dog carries a pulsing ring (red once it's in reach). When one gets close,
time snaps into slow-mo and a click **smacks** it back toward whatever you're looking at — vendors, or the boss.
The soundtrack is procedural (a 16-step lookahead sequencer) and arranged per pier: xylophone pop on the Boardwalk,
a swung ice-cream-truck calypso with marimba and bells on Sunset Pier, a slow dreamy minor-pentatonic bell piece with
a synth pad for the Night Market, a circus oom-pah organ with tuba and chord stabs on Storm Pier, and a double-time
rush with an octave-doubled lead for the finale. It muffles as time slows and speeds up in the boss zone. Vendors yell at you in autotune (word-by-word speech synthesis snapped to a pentatonic
scale with a synth harmony underneath); one vendor sings at a time, each word lands on a beat of the music, and only
vendors within ~24 m are audible. Your arm stays off-screen and jabs in from the bottom-right on a punch.

# Miles Morales: Brooklyn Nights

A fan-made, browser-based web-swinging game starring Miles Morales. Swing across a
night-time Brooklyn skyline, wall-crawl up buildings, and stop rooftop crimes with
punches, Venom Strikes and camouflage stealth takedowns.

Everything in the game (art, sound effects, physics, city generation) is written in
plain JavaScript on an HTML5 canvas. There are no dependencies, no build step and no
external assets.

Four games live in this repo:

- `index.html` – the original 2D side-scrolling game (no dependencies at all).
- `3d.html` – **Brooklyn Nights 3D**: a third-person, fully 3D remake built on
  Three.js. Same hero, same moves, but you swing through a procedurally generated
  city block grid, wall-crawl real towers and fight on rooftops in 3D. After the
  8th crime the Rhino shows up for a boss fight, then Venom, the Spot, and the Prowler. Beat him
  and Act II opens: the Sinister Ten, ten more rogues in a random order. The city is rendered with real-time
  sun shadows, sky reflections, textured facades with recessed windows, storefronts,
  parapets, water towers, trees, street lamps, crosswalks and traffic.
- `spiderman2.html` – **Spider-Man 2: Brooklyn Nights**, the sequel. Two playable
  Spider-Men, a bigger two-borough city split by the East River, web wings, wind
  tunnels, slingshot pads, parrying, Kraven's hunters and a three-boss campaign
  (the Lizard, Kraven, Venom). See [Spider-Man 2](#spider-man-2-brooklyn-nights) below.
- `rocket.html` – **Rocket Run 3D**: something completely different. Pilot a rocket
  across an alien canyon world, hopping from launch pad to launch pad, flying through
  rings and setting it down gently on the beacon. See [Rocket Run 3D](#rocket-run-3d)
  below.

## Spider-Man 2: Brooklyn Nights

Open `spiderman2.html`. It is built on the 3D engine, so everything from Brooklyn
Nights 3D (swinging, wall-crawling, web shots, the comic look, the radio, the PWA)
carries over. What is new:

### Two Spider-Men

You start as **Peter Parker** with **Miles Morales** swinging beside you as your AI
partner. Press `Tab` (SWAP on touch) at any moment to trade places: the partner's
body becomes the one you drive and your old hero drops into the partner role. Each
hero keeps his own health, his own power meter and his own suits, and the benched
hero slowly heals, so swapping out when you are low is a real tactic.

# games-operator

Game streaming on Kubernetes. One Go binary is a **Moonlight-compatible host**: your Moonlight clients (Android, iOS, TV, PC) or a browser via [moonlight-web](https://github.com/linckosz/moonlight-web) pair with it, see your apps, and press play. Each app (Steam, Firefox, RetroArch, a launcher, any Games on Whales image) runs as its **own pod** next to [Wolf](https://games-on-whales.github.io/wolf/) on the GPU node while someone streams, with its own home volume, and is gone when the stream ends.

It is the sibling of [agents-operator](https://github.com/dseif0x/agents-operator) and a cleaner successor to [fenrir](https://github.com/games-on-whales/fenrir): no CRDs, apps are rows users create in a web UI, several apps can stream at the same time on one LoadBalancer IP.

```
Moonlight client ──47989/47984──▶ hub (Moonlight protocol: pair, applist, launch)
                 ──RTSP/RTP/ENet─▶ app pod: app + wolf (with its own PulseAudio) + wolf-bridge
browser ─▶ hub (/play, reverse proxy) ─▶ moonlight-web (embedded) ─▶ (same path, re-packetised onto WebRTC or a WebSocket)
hub ──▶ Postgres (users, apps, pairings)   hub ──▶ Kubernetes (pods, PVCs, Services)
```

- **Hub** (`cmd/games-operator`): web UI + REST API, the Moonlight HTTP/HTTPS front door, a level-triggered reconciler that turns app rows into pods, and a Wolf-compatible pairing API so moonlight-web pairs without typing a PIN.
- **wolf-bridge** (`cmd/wolf-bridge`): sidecar that exposes Wolf's unix socket API to the hub with a per-launch token and tells the hub whether a client is streaming (idle stop).
- **Apps**: created from presets (Steam, Firefox, Prism Launcher, RetroArch, Lutris, Heroic, Pegasus, custom image) with the launch wrapper, capabilities and devices that are known to work.
- **Streams**: every running app gets its own port set (`48100+10×slot …`) on the IP the Moonlight Service uses (MetalLB `allow-shared-ip` / Cilium sharing key), so N users can play N apps at once.
- **Users**: admins define a **catalog** of apps and manage accounts and quotas; users add catalog apps to their own list, each with its own home volume, and pair their own Moonlight clients. Every user sees only their apps, in the hub and in Moonlight.

Details: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [docs/OPERATIONS.md](docs/OPERATIONS.md), chart values in [charts/games-operator/values.yaml](charts/games-operator/values.yaml).

# 十步万度 · Ten Steps, Ten Thousand Degrees

一个 5×5 箭头小游戏，以及它背后的转子路由 / 沙堆群数学。
A 5×5 arrow-rotation puzzle and the rotor-router / sandpile-group mathematics behind it.

**在线地址 · Live pages**

| | 地址 · URL |
|---|---|
| 原版游戏 · Original game | <https://youhuali.github.io/ten-steps-ten-thousand-degrees/> |
| 群论演示 · Group-theory demo | <https://youhuali.github.io/ten-steps-ten-thousand-degrees/demo/> |

---

## 游戏规则 · Rules

棋盘是 5×5 的格子，每格有一个箭头，初始全部朝上。点击一格，它的箭头顺时针转 90°；若转后指向棋盘内的另一格，该格也转 90°，如此连锁，直到箭头指向棋盘外为止。每次旋转记 90°，原版给 10 次点击机会，目标是累计一万度。

The board is a 5×5 grid of arrows, all pointing up at the start. Clicking a cell rotates its arrow 90° clockwise; if the arrow now points at another cell, that cell rotates too, and the chain continues until an arrow points off the board. Each rotation scores 90°. The original game allows 10 clicks and asks for 10,000 degrees.

## 主要结论 · Main results

| 中文 | English |
|---|---|
| 总度数只依赖点击的多重集，与顺序无关（阿贝尔性质，Diaconis–Fulton / 最小作用原理证明）。 | The total score depends only on the multiset of clicks, not their order (abelian property; proof via the odometer / least-action principle). |
| 局面与沙堆群 $S(G)=\mathbb{Z}^{25}/\mathbb{Z}^{25}\Delta'$ 的元素一一对应，群的阶为 32,565,539,635,200，结构为 $\mathbb{Z}_4\oplus\mathbb{Z}_{16}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_{48}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_{102960}^2$。 | Board states correspond bijectively to elements of the sandpile group $S(G)=\mathbb{Z}^{25}/\mathbb{Z}^{25}\Delta'$, of order 32,565,539,635,200 and type $\mathbb{Z}_4\oplus\mathbb{Z}_{16}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_{48}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_{102960}^2$. |
| 10 步最高 10,800°，恰有两个最优方案；平均每步得分在 10 步时达到峰值。 | The 10-click maximum is 10,800°, attained by exactly two multisets; the per-click average peaks at 10 clicks. |
| 单位元的最少点击代表需要 20 次，恰有 3 个；中心点击一次的逆元最少 19 次。 | The cheapest click representatives of the identity use 20 clicks (exactly three of them); the inverse of one center click needs 19 clicks. |
| 中心点击的阶是 104，角格的阶是 102,960（群的指数）。 | A center click has order 104; a corner click has order 102,960, the exponent of the group. |

| `demo/` | 群论演示页：不限步数、施加单位元、施加逆元 · Interactive demo: unlimited clicks, apply an identity, apply the inverse |
| `PROOF.md` | 次序无关的证明与群论视角 · Proof of order-independence and the group-theoretic view |
| `reference.md` / `reference.pdf` | 沙堆群参考笔记（4 点图例子、三种理解方式、最少单位元代表） · Sandpile-group notes (4-vertex example, three descriptions, minimal identity) |

# Forest Motion: Jetson gesture control

A local Python hand-control prototype for the project in [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md).
MediaPipe detects hand landmarks; adjustable control logic moves a character inside
a top-down forest arena. Both hands are supported. The hand faces the camera, palm
out. Default controls use **open hand for up, fist for down, index-thumb pinch for
left, and pinkie-thumb pinch for right**. A partially relaxed hand stops movement.
A second mode uses four thumb-to-finger
touches. The three-level web game ends with a projected virtual boss in Boss Arena.

## Jetson setup

### Ethan's web game with MediaPipe GPU controls

The web game in `game/fight/debug.html` consumes the same UDP movement packets
produced by this controller. No model conversion is needed: select GPU when
starting the Python controller. Run all three processes on the Jetson; the page
currently connects to `ws://localhost:8765`, so open it in the Jetson's browser.

From the repository root, update and install the web relay once (Node.js/npm required):

```bash
git pull origin main
npm ci --prefix game/fight
```

Terminal 1, from the repository root, starts the UDP-to-WebSocket relay:

```bash
node game/fight/relay.mjs
```

Terminal 2, from the repository root, starts GPU hand detection and sends controls
to the relay's UDP port 5005:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python3 -u -m gesture_control --headless --inference-device gpu --camera 0 --udp-port 5005
```

Use `--camera 1` for a different webcam. **Headless mode opens no Python demo or
camera-preview window**; Ethan's browser page is the game. A compatible saved
calibration is loaded automatically. Otherwise follow the three terminal prompts:
relaxed fingers, fist, then open hand. Press Enter to start each recording. Failed
poses retry without discarding completed recordings. Keep this process running
while playing; only one process should open the webcam. Terminal commands require
Enter: `c` recalibrates, `p` pauses/resumes, `q` quits. Ctrl+C also stops and sends
a zero-movement packet. Use `--calibrate` to force fresh terminal calibration.
Headless mode defaults to UDP port 5005 when `--udp-port` is omitted.

Terminal 3, from the repository root, serves the game:

```bash
python3 -u -m game.serve
```

Open **http://localhost:8000/debug.html** in the Jetson browser, then press B to
start. Open palm = up, fist = down, index-thumb pinch = left, pinkie-thumb pinch =
right. The game HUD displays gesture/link status.

Wick

A daily word game where you guess by meaning, not spelling.

Play in your browser · App Store · Website · Privacy · Report a bug

--- There is one secret word a day. Type any word and Wick tells you how close you are in meaning: freezing, cold, cool, warm, hot, boiling. "Tomato" is hot when the answer is "red". "Tomb" is freezing, even though the letters look close. No letter clues, no colored tiles. You can also ask Wick, the little flame who guards the word, yes or no questions, and it answers without ever giving the word away. The iOS app and the web game play the same daily puzzle, in English, Spanish, French, Italian and German. Single player on iOS runs entirely on the phone. Live races and the web game are scored by a small server, and that server is the only place a secret lives: one Google Gemini API key, read from its environment. This repository is all three parts.

# Cyberpunk-Txt-RPG
Game designed to be within the universe of cyberpunk 2077, text based RPG, with in depth mechanics.

**▶ Play it: https://wh173-0u7.github.io/Cyberpunk-Txt-RPG/** (the stable release, from `main`)

**▶ Try the beta: https://wh173-0u7.github.io/Cyberpunk-Txt-RPG/beta/** (the next version, from `beta`; it keeps a save of its own, so it never touches the stable game's)

It runs in the browser so the text can be surrounded by neon glow, CRT scanlines, glitch effects,
weather particles and screen effects that react to what's happening in the game.

## Running it

You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20 or newer.

```bash
npm install      # once
npm run dev      # starts the game at http://localhost:5173 and reloads on every save
```

Other scripts:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | Runs the unit tests (game logic, plus checks on 500 generated cities) |
| `npm run typecheck` | Checks the TypeScript for errors |
| `npm run build` | Builds a static site into `dist/` that can be hosted anywhere (e.g. GitHub Pages); `CHANNEL=beta` builds the beta, with its own save |

Branches and releases: new work goes to `beta` by pull request, and a push to `beta` or `main`
rebuilds both sites (the beta under `/beta/`, the stable release at the root) and deploys them.
When the beta is good, merge `beta` into `main` and run the **Release** workflow from the Actions
tab with the version (e.g. `0.2.0`): it tags `main` as `v0.2.0` and publishes a GitHub Release
with the notes since the last one and the built site as a zip. Settings says which build you're
on.

## Playing

Every game is a new, procedurally generated Night City: a different mix of districts
(Watson, Westbrook, City Center, Heywood, Santo Domingo, Pacifica, sometimes the Badlands),
different places in them, weather and streets.

**Canon first.** Districts sit where they are in the real Night City (Watson north, City
Center in the middle, Westbrook east, Heywood and Santo Domingo south, Pacifica south-west,

# fantasy-dash

Dashboard for the Husky Fantasy Sleeper league. Static site, data refreshed weekly.

## Layout

- `packages/core` - Sleeper client, normalizer, stats engine, schemas (pure TypeScript)
- `packages/web` - Vite + React app
- `scripts/sync.ts` - pulls every season from Sleeper into `data/`
- `data/` - generated JSON, committed
- `docs/superpowers/specs` - design spec; `docs/superpowers/plans` - implementation plans

## Commands

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm sync          # refresh data/ from Sleeper (about 2 minutes)
pnpm sync:dry      # same, but writes to a temp dir
pnpm test          # all packages
pnpm dev           # web dev server
pnpm build         # production build to packages/web/dist
```

## Deploy

`.github/workflows/sync.yml` runs every Tuesday morning, on manual dispatch, and on every push to `main`. Scheduled and manual runs sync, test, commit `data/`, build, and deploy to GitHub Pages; push runs skip the sync and only test, build, and deploy. One-time setup in the GitHub repo: Settings, Pages, Source = GitHub Actions.

GitHub disables scheduled workflows after 60 days without repository activity. In the off-season, run the workflow manually once in a while or push a commit to keep the Tuesday sync alive.

## Config

`league.config.ts` holds the league ID, display name, and optional manager display-name overrides.

# Vocana Compat

Companion mod for [Vocana](https://github.com/slappyfish167/Vocana) (NeoForge 21.1, Minecraft 1.21.1): soft-dependency
bridges that teach Vocana's spoken language new words from other mods' worlds and let their gear, slots and magic
systems talk to the Seal. Nothing here is required by Vocana; each bridge is a **module** that only loads when its
mod is installed, and every module can be switched off.

| Module | Mod | Toggle (`config/vocanacompat-modules.toml`) | Own settings |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create | `create` 6.0.x | `modules.create.enabled` | `config/vocanacompat-create.toml` |
| Wyrmroost | `wyrmroost` 1.4.x (NeoForge port) | `modules.wyrmroost.enabled` | `config/vocanacompat-wyrmroost.toml` |
| Ice and Fire: Community Edition | `iceandfire` 2.1.x | `modules.iceandfire.enabled` | `config/vocanacompat-iceandfire.toml` |
| EMI | `emi` 1.1.x | `modules.emi.enabled` | `config/vocanacompat-emi.toml` |
| Curios API | `curios` 9.5.x | `modules.curios.enabled` | `config/vocanacompat-curios.toml` |
| Hex Casting (HexCast NEOFORGED) | `hexcasting` 0.11.x | `modules.hexcasting.enabled` | `config/vocanacompat-hexcasting.toml` |
| Ars Nouveau | `ars_nouveau` 5.13.x | `modules.ars_nouveau.enabled` | `config/vocanacompat-ars_nouveau.toml` |

All toggles default to on. A module that is off registers nothing, and its data (recipes, tags, words) stays out of
the game through the `vocanacompat:module_enabled` condition. Version 1.0.0 is the skeleton: the modules exist and
load, their content is being filled in (see `CHANGELOG.md`).

## Install

Requires Vocana 2.1.0 or later and NeoForge 21.1.255 or later on Minecraft 1.21.1. Drop `vocana-compat-<version>.jar`
in `mods/` next to Vocana and whichever of the seven mods you play with. It runs on both sides; a client without it
can join a server that has it only if the loaded modules add nothing the client must know (words are server-side,
but Curios slots and EMI pages are not), so install it on both.

## Build

The build needs Vocana in your local maven, because Vocana publishes no public artifact:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/slappyfish167/Vocana.git && cd Vocana
git checkout "$(cat ../Vocana-Compat/vocana.ref)"     # the Vocana ref this skeleton was built against
./gradlew publishToMavenLocal -x test                  # publishes dev.vocana:vocana:<version>
cd ../Vocana-Compat
./gradlew build                                        # jar in build/libs, unit tests
./gradlew runGameTestServer

# Sword of Harkinian

Sword Kirby as the player character in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, running on
[Ship of Harkinian](https://github.com/HarbourMasters/Shipwright).

Kirby's sword ability is already Link in everything but shape: he wears the green cap
and swings a blade. Ocarina of Time's player skeleton turns out to meet him most of the
way, because the cap and the sheathed sword are each their own bone. The costume is
mostly a matter of replacing the ball underneath.

## Status

He plays. Both ages pack into one `.o2r` archive each that Ship of Harkinian 9.3.0 loads
from its `mods` folder, with the sheathed sword and shield on the back of the ball, the
sword held blade up beside him, the shield at his side when raised, mittens on every empty
hand, and the pause screen's Equipment page posed to match.

| Piece | State |
| --- | --- |
| Link's limb table, derived from extracted game data | Done, and verified against the real import |
| Asset extraction from the ROM | Done, `decomp/extracted/ntsc-1.2` |
| Fast64 skeleton import of both ages | Done, 21 bones, table agrees |
| Sword Kirby, assembled and rigged to the real skeleton | Done, 490 vertices, 706 triangles |
| Packing into an `.o2r` the port reads from `mods` | Done, `tools/make_mod.py` |
| Every player animation re-posed for his arms, legs and sheath | Done, `tools/carry_fk.py` |
| Running it in Ship of Harkinian 9.3.0 on Windows (DirectX 11) and macOS (Metal) | Done |

![Standing](docs/preview/final_idle_front.png)
![Guarding](docs/preview/final_guard_front.png)
![Sword out](docs/preview/final_sword_behind.png)

## Installing the mod

1. Download `SwordKirby-1.0.0.zip` from the releases page, or build it yourself (below).
2. Unzip it and copy `kirby_child.o2r` and `kirby_adult.o2r` into Ship of Harkinian's
   `mods` folder, the one beside `oot.o2r` that holds `custom_mod_files_go_here.txt`.
3. Start the game. Nothing to enable; the archives replace Link's model, hands, sheath
   and animations by name, and deleting them puts him back.

The zip also carries `kirby_voice.o2r`, which is optional at install time and gives him
Kirby's voice from Super Smash Bros. in place of Link's; copy it into the same folder or
leave it out. `tools/kirby_voice_map.py` is how it is built.

```powershell
python ..\.claude\skills\mod-zip\zip_mod.py --config tools/mod_zip.json
```
